title: CDSCO Warns Against 2 Beauty Creams Over Excessive Heavy Metals
summary: New Delhi: The Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation (CDSCO) has issued a public health alert advising consumers against purchasing or using Goree Beauty Cream and Chandni Whitening Cream, both...

contentHtml:
The CDSCO said the products had not been issued registration certificates by the competent authority for import and sale in India. It warned that the excessive heavy metals may pose health risks to consumers, including toxic effects.

In its public notice, the CDSCO said cosmetic products used by consumers must be safe. It stated that the manufacture and import of cosmetics are regulated under the Drugs and Cosmetics Act, 1940, and the Cosmetics Rules, 2020, while standards for cosmetic products are published by the Bureau of Indian Standards. A licence from the State Licensing Authority is required to manufacture cosmetics for sale and distribution, and imported cosmetics must be registered with the Central Licensing Authority.

The CDSCO advised consumers not to purchase the two named products and not to use them or similarly named cosmetic products if already purchased.It also advised the public to purchase and use authorised cosmetics bearing the manufacturing licence number, manufacturer’s details, batch number, manufacturing and expiry dates, and, in the case of imported cosmetics, the registration number. Labelling violations should be reported to the respective State Drugs Controller for products manufactured in India and to the Drugs Controller General (India) for imported products, the notice said.

The notice stated that the products are unauthorised and contatns excessive heavy metals beyondthe specified limits which may pose health risk to the consumers including toxic effects

ln light of the above unauthorised cosmetics products, consumers are advised to:

- Not to purchase above mentioned cosmetics products

- Not to use such & similar named cosmetic products if purchased
